posts.title: Welcome to the WPBRC Blog
posts.author: WPBRC
posts.excerpt: A new place for clear, non-partisan updates on the development projects, public meetings, and decisions shaping West Palm Beach.
posts.body:
Welcome to the West Palm Beach Residents Coalition blog. This is where we’ll share clear, non-partisan updates on the issues that affect our whole city — new development projects, upcoming public meetings and hearings, and the long-term planning decisions that shape our neighborhoods.

What to expect

Each week we’ll summarize what’s moving on the development tracker, flag the meetings worth showing up for, and explain what it means for residents — in plain language, with sources.

Stay in the loop

Prefer it in your inbox? Sign up for our newsletter, and consider joining the Coalition to add your voice.

posts.title: What’s rising across West Palm Beach: a development snapshot
posts.author: WPBRC
posts.excerpt: From the Flagler Drive towers to the SoSo and Northwood corridors, here is a high-level look at the projects we are tracking citywide.
posts.body:
Our development tracker now follows dozens of major projects across West Palm Beach — completed, under construction, approved, proposed, and on hold. Here’s a brief snapshot of the landscape.

The waterfront keeps building up

North and South Flagler Drive continue to see a wave of residential towers. These projects bring investment and new residents, but also raise real questions about traffic, density, and public access to the water — exactly the citywide issues the Coalition follows.

Downtown and the corridors

Downtown, CityPlace, and the Dixie Highway corridor (including SoSo) are adding offices, hotels, and mixed-use space, while Northwood and the North End see large redevelopments. Use the map to filter by status and district to see what’s near you.

This is a working summary; verify specifics against current City of West Palm Beach agendas. See the full, filterable map on the Development page.
